Both sections (accommodation and meals) still contain two occurrences of L('<slot>', lang) — one IIFE in the section header and one named const inside the map — violating the AC requirement of 'at most once' per section.

ac_results.evidence: FAIL. Accommodation section: L('accommodation', lang) appears at lines 2413 AND 2416 — two occurrences. Line 2413: section-header IIFE '(() => { const accLabel = L("accommodation", lang); return accLabel !== "accommodation" ? ... })()' — original IIFE left intact (only renamed v→accLabel inside). Line 2416: 'const accLabel = L("accommodation", lang)' — new named const inside .map() callback. The card-body IIFE (originally at line ~2454) was eliminated and replaced by accLabel reference at line 2445. Net result: 1 IIFE + 1 const = 2 calls to L('accommodation', lang) in the accommodation section. AC requires 'at most once'. Meals section: identical pattern — line 2468 IIFE and line 2471 const mealsLabel = L('meals', lang) — 2 occurrences. AC requires at most once per section. The deduplication was partial: the card-body IIFE was eliminated but the section-header IIFE was not folded into the named const. A correct fix would extract const accLabel = L('accommodation', lang) ABOVE the section header div (before line 2412) and use it in both the header and the map body, eliminating the header IIFE entirely.
ac_results.recommendation: Extract const accLabel = L('accommodation', lang) as a single declaration before the section header <div> (before line 2412). Replace the section-header IIFE at line 2413 with a direct reference to accLabel. The map body at line 2416 should then delete its own const accLabel declaration and use the outer-scope accLabel. Same pattern for mealsLabel. This produces exactly one L() call per section.
